nodes.name: Ni-Fe PBA Nanocubes Synthesis
nodes.procedure: In a typical synthesis procedure, 698 mg of nickel (II) nitrate hexahydrate and 882 mg of sodium citrate tribasic dihydrate were fully dissolved in 80 ml of deionized water using sonication, forming solution A. Meanwhile, 528 mg of potassium hexacyanoferrate (III) was dissolved in 120 ml of deionized water to prepare solution B. Solution B was then swiftly combined with solution A in 15 s under magnetic stirring, followed by 1 min of additional stirring. The mixture was left to stand at room temperature for 24 hours. The resulting yellow precipitate was harvested through repeated cycles of centrifugation and washing with deionized water and ethanol. Finally, the products were dried overnight in a vacuum oven at 70°C.

nodes.name: Ni-Fe PBA Nanocages Synthesis
nodes.procedure: To synthesize the Ni-Fe PBA nanocages, an acid etching method assisted by tannic acid (TA) was utilized. Initially, 20 mg of as-synthesized Ni-Fe PBA nanocubes and 1200 mg of TA were thoroughly dissolved in 40 ml of isopropanol assisted by sonication. Subsequently, 10 ml of a 1 M hydrochloric acid solution was added to this mixture. The resulting solution was then transferred to a Teflon-lined stainless-steel autoclave and heated at 140°C for 6 hours. The product was obtained through multiple cycles of centrifugation and washing with ethanol, followed by overnight drying in a vacuum oven at 70°C.

nodes.name: Ni-Fe-P Nanocages Phosphatization
nodes.procedure: 20 mg of Ni-Fe PBA nanocages and 200 mg of NaH2PO2 powder were placed in two separate porcelain boats within a tube furnace, with the nanocages positioned downstream and the NaH2PO2 powder upstream. The samples were heated at 350°C for 1 to 2 hours at a rate of 5°C per minute under a nitrogen atmosphere. After the treatment, the samples were allowed to cool to room temperature while still under nitrogen protection before being collected.

nodes.evidence_snippet: Extended x-ray absorption fine structure (EXAFS) spectroscopy analyses confirm the phosphide structure of Ni-Fe-P nanocages, with coordination numbers of 2.1 and 1.9 for the innermost coordination shells, corresponding to Fe-P bonds with bond lengths of 2.20 and 2.35 Å respectively (Fig. 1, H and I; fig. S7; and table S1)

nodes.characterization_summary: XPS reveals conversion to O-M-P structure with P 2p binding energy of 131.7 eV; O 1s peak shifts from 531.0 eV (M-OH) to 530.0 eV (M-O); Fe 2p shows decrease at ~704.0 eV (Fe-P) and increase at ~710.0 eV (Fe-O).
nodes.evidence_snippet: XPS spectra in the P 2p region reveal a conversion to the O-M-P structure with a binding energy of 131.7 eV after exposing the catalyst to the OER (fig. S16A). The O 1s peak at 531.0 eV shifts to 530.0 eV after OER, indicating the conversion from M-OH to M-O bindings (Fig. 2G). XPS analysis in the Fe 2p region reveals a clear decrease in peak intensity at ~704.0 eV (Fe-P bonds) alongside an increase at ~710.0 eV (Fe-O bonds) (Fig. 2H)

nodes.characterization_summary: Operando Q-XAFS reveals preferential oxidation of Fe sites forming O-Fe-P structure; Fe-O coordination reaches 15-20% while Ni-P remains largely intact in first CV cycle.
nodes.evidence_snippet: approximately 15% of the Fe-P local structure is converted to Fe-O, while the Ni-P structure remains intact... The Fe-O coordination percentage increases to about 20% of the total Fe-O/P coordination in the first coordination shell
